resources.string: The Music tab, its artwork sources and playback.
The Music tab in the navigation bar. Turning it off hides the tab and stops the player; your library and settings are kept.
Adds HD logos, banners, backgrounds and CD art. A free personal key from fanart.tv (Account, Your API keys). Applies the next time an artist is added or refreshed.

Artist tags and ladder suggestions from Last.fm instead of MusicBrainz, which is often slow or unreachable. A free key from last.fm/api/account/create. MusicBrainz is still used when Last.fm has no answer.
Biographies, logos and backgrounds. Without a key the shared test key is used, which is rate limited. Applies the next time an artist is added or refreshed.
On an artist page, finds where to go next without being asked. Turn off on a slow connection; the page then waits for a button.

Tries the redesigned album page: the cover and artist in the header, and tabs that change what the two side panels show (Song by song first; more to come). Needs a wide window. Off keeps the current page.

Tries the redesigned artist page: a photo hero with Play Essentials, then three panels below it (about the artist or the song you are on, the Essentials and Discography tabs, and your library). Needs a wide window. Off keeps the current page.

Tries the quick-play first screen for Music: type an artist, album, song or remix with the on-screen letter strip (the likely next letters light up and move beside the one you pressed), a keyboard or your voice, and YouTube Music and YouTube are searched together. Your library stays underneath. Off keeps the current Music tab.
Skips the spoken intros, skits and outros in music videos, as marked by SponsorBlock users. Videos are looked up by a short hash prefix, so SponsorBlock never learns what you play.

Another addon to ask when the ones above do not have an album, such as NullBeat Lite. They are asked in order, and the first that has the album plays it. Private to you and not included in settings backups.
With a link, an album page can play a lossless copy from your addon instead of YouTube Music. Paste your addon's manifest link. It is private to you and is not included in settings backups.
Prefer the addon when it has the album
Albums open on the addon's lossless copy when it has one; the switch on the album page still lets you pick YouTube Music.
Holds the Music pages still: no drifting backgrounds, pulsing, cycling or spinning disc.

MusicBrainz's web service answers one request a second and often turns requests away, which slows artist pages and "Where next?". An offline copy answers instantly. About 3 GB to download, then about ten minutes of building in the background; it keeps about 2 GB.
Building the index, %1$d%%. The app stays usable meanwhile.
Dump of %1$s: %2$s artists, %3$s release groups, %4$s on disk.

Community-submitted lyrics timed to the syllable (the database behind Better Lyrics). A lookup sends the song\'s title and artist to unison.betterlyrics.org. Turned on, lyrics are asked for when a track first plays and remembered on this computer.
An open collection of community-timed lyrics in the style of Apple Music. A lookup sends the song\'s title and artist to api.amll.dev.
Word-timed lyrics from Netease\'s unofficial interface; it may not answer outside China. A lookup sends the song\'s title and artist to music.163.com.

The widest reach: a third-party service that relays other catalogues\' lyrics and does not state its terms, so it is off until you turn it on. A lookup sends the song\'s title, artist and length to api.lrcmux.dev.

Syllable-timed lyrics from Apple Music, fetched through a third-party service that does not state its terms, so it is off until you turn it on. A lookup sends the song\'s title, artist and length to lyricsplus.binimum.org.
Fill album facts in the background

Writes Liner Notes, track notes and song stories for your whole library ahead of time, most played albums first, so an album opens with its facts already there. Uses your own AI key; nothing is sent until you switch this on. It waits while a film is playing.

The most tokens the filler uses from your AI key in 24 hours. A free Groq key allows 200,000 a day and 8,000 a minute, shared with everything else you ask it, so the default leaves some for you. Press to change. The filler also spaces its lookups to stay under the minute limit, and pauses by itself if it hits a limit.
Asks again now for the lookups listed below, instead of waiting the two hours after which they are tried again by themselves.
Looks at every album on the next pass instead of skipping the ones already finished. Nothing already written is asked for twice.
Saves the facts the AI wrote and your own pins to a JSON file you can keep or give to someone. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Adds the facts from a file someone gave you. It only fills gaps: nothing you already have, and none of your own pins, is replaced. You see what it would add first, and can undo it afterwards.
